37 The circuit diagram shows a battery with internal resistance r, two resistors, a switch and a
voltmeter. The switch is open.
r
V
The switch is now closed.
What happens to the current in the battery, and what happens to the reading on the voltmeter,
when the switch is closed?
current in battery
reading on voltmeter
A
increases
decreases
B
increases
remains the same
C
remains the same
decreases
D
remains the same
remains the same

hints: Notice the voltmeter is connected across the battery terminals and the two resistors are connected between the same two points when the switch closes.
Recall that closing the switch places the second resistor in parallel with the first, so the combined external resistance $R$ decreases.
Recall terminal p.d. is $V = E - Ir$, so think what a larger battery current $I$ does to the lost volts $Ir$ and to $V$.
walkthrough: Identify the circuit: with the switch open only one resistor is across the battery, with the switch closed two resistors are in parallel across the same two points where voltmeter $V$ is connected.
State the resistance rule: two resistors in parallel have a smaller combined resistance than either alone, so external resistance $R$ decreases when the switch is closed.
State the current rule: total resistance is $R+r$ and battery current is $I = E/(R+r)$, so a smaller $R$ gives a larger $I$ - current in the battery increases.
State the terminal p.d. rule: voltmeter reads $V = E - Ir$, where $Ir$ is the p.d. lost across internal resistance $r$.
Connect the result: larger $I$ means larger $Ir$, so $V$ decreases even though $E$ is constant. This is option A.

A.explanation: Closing the switch adds a second resistor in parallel so external resistance falls, battery current rises and lost volts $Ir$ rises, so terminal $V = E - Ir$ falls.

B.explanation: Battery current does increase, but terminal p.d. cannot stay equal to $E$ because the larger current increases the drop $Ir$ across internal resistance $r$.

C.explanation: Battery current does not stay the same because the parallel combination has lower resistance than one resistor alone, so total current $I = E/(R+r)$ must increase.

D.explanation: Both change because lower external resistance increases total current and therefore increases lost volts, reducing the voltmeter reading.
